blocker.summary: ROOT CAUSE FOUND, closing the entire r399-r448 investigation chain, and it connects to an already-documented finding from much earlier in the campaign (r240/r241/r275, long before r399). r447 had mis-concluded that the dispatch target 0x823D035C was real guest code (it fell within the .text address range); r448 corrected this immediately upon finding Ghidra's disassembler failed there ('Bad instruction data') while spontaneously naming the location 'NtReadFile' -- it's a kernel import table slot, not PPC code. This project's tools/materialize_native_import_stubs.py already has a detailed, previously-instrumented NtReadFile stub (predating r399) whose own comments already documented this exact failure: 'the PAC path still fails with handle=0x829xxxxx (image FILE_OBJECT, not small HANDLE) and offset=0xfefefefe (stack garbage, not 0)', citing the same globals (0x82758EB0, 0x8293B930/94C/938) and the same functions (sub_821D5F48, sub_821CC508) this session's r436-r446 independently rediscovered via live gdb tracing. Running with AC6_NATIVE_IMPORT_TRACE=1 (already supported, never used this session) confirmed it exactly live: handle=0x82918a78 (a FILE_OBJECT pointer, not a real HANDLE), offset=4278124286=0xFEFEFEFE (the uninitialized-fill pattern), queue@0x829ddd80 (the same descriptor r443-r446 tracked). The stub correctly refuses to fabricate STATUS_SUCCESS (returns STATUS_INVALID_HANDLE instead) rather than risk corrupting PAC data -- a decision already made and documented by an earlier cycle, still correct. Full causal chain, each link now evidence-backed: bad arguments -> NtReadFile correctly fails -> sub_821CC508 exhausts 5 retries (r446) -> sub_821D5F48 fails, never constructs the renderer object at 0x82935D98 (r436-r441) -> sub_821D7DE0 logs non-fatally and proceeds anyway (r442) -> sub_821D6C20 dereferences the null object unguarded -> SIGSEGV (r435-r436). Not yet established: WHY the handle/offset are wrong -- a codegen bug in argument preparation somewhere upstream, or a genuinely missing initialization step in this offline environment. The lr/backchain capture attempted this cycle returned all-zero return addresses (PPC_CONFIG_SKIP_LR, already noted in the stub's own comments) so it did not resolve the true caller. Named for r449: static disassembly around the actual NtReadFile call site inside sub_821CC508/sub_821D5F48 (already located) to determine which. The native_vulkan_backend.cpp backlog commit decision (r433/r434/r438) remains the other open, user-dependent thread.
